mainTopic: Who may testify about the new moon: relatives, disqualified witnesses, breaking שבת to testify, and the start of the second chapter on unknown witnesses
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story from the previous משנה. A ברייתא says it was זפר, the head of גדר, and not רבי עקיבא, who held back the forty pairs of witnesses, and רבן גמליאל removed him from office. A new משנה teaches that relatives cannot form a pair of witnesses for the new moon, but רבי שמעון says they are valid. רבי יוסי supports the first view with the story of טוביה הרופא, whose son was rejected by the בית דין. The גמרא gives רבי לוי's source for רבי שמעון, 'החודש הזה לכם', said to the brothers משה and אהרן, and then shows how the רבנן read the same פסוק. רב חנן בר רבא rules like רבי שמעון, but רב הונא shows that רב's silence actually backed the other view, while שמואל rules like רבי שמעון. The next משנה lists people who are not valid witnesses and compares them to a woman, and רב אשי learns from this that a גזלן דדבריהם may testify in עדות אשה. The chapter ends with witnesses breaking שבת to reach בית דין. The new chapter opens with the rule that an unknown witness needs someone to vouch for him, a תקנה made because of the בייתוסים. The גמרא begins asking what 'another' means, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה's story of the forty pairs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה about more than forty pairs of witnesses whom רבי עקיבא held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: There was a story where more than forty pairs of witnesses were passing through, and רבי עקיבא held them back, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can comment on it. This is a setup line for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא held back many witnesses from breaking שבת to travel and testify about the new moon. The גמרא brings up this line because a ברייתא tells the story differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident that really happened
He held them back or stopped them
'Etc.', meaning the quote continues in the source

phrases.english: There was an incident where more than forty pairs passed through
phrases.notes: These are pairs of witnesses heading to ירושלים to testify that they saw the new moon.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva detained them, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ יוֹתֵר מֵאַרְבָּעִים זוּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה reports that רבי עקיבא held back more than forty pairs of witnesses.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says it was really זפר of גדר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: it was not רבי עקיבא who held back the witnesses but זפר, the head of גדר, and רבן גמליאל had him removed from office.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, Heaven forbid that רבי עקיבא held them back! Rather, it was זפר, the head of גדר, who held them back. רבן גמליאל sent word, and they removed him from his high position.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells the story from the משנה differently. רבי יהודה insists that someone else, not רבי עקיבא, held back the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה cannot accept that a great sage like רבי עקיבא would stop witnesses from coming to testify. He gives the act to a local leader, זפר. The fact that רבן גמליאל removed him from office shows that holding back the witnesses was treated as a serious wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught', which introduces a ברייתא
The head (leader) of the town of גדר

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a halachic argument about whether witnesses should travel. It is a disagreement about who actually held them back.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Heaven forbid that Rabbi Akiva detained them!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שַׁזְפַּר רֹאשָׁהּ שֶׁל גֶּדֶר עִיכְּבָן,
phrases.english: Rather, Zefer, the head of Geder, detained them,
and Rabban Gamliel sent word,
and they removed him from his high office.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the story the משנה told
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, זפר, the head of גדר, held back the witnesses, and רבן גמליאל had him removed from office.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the one who held back the witnesses was זפר of גדר, not רבי עקיבא. He was removed from office for it.

steps.title: A father and son who saw the moon should both go
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a father and son who saw the new moon should both go. They cannot be paired together, but if one is disqualified, the other can pair with another witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A father and his son who saw the new moon should both go. This is not because they can join together as a pair. It is because if one of them is disqualified, the second can join with a different witness.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה teaches that relatives who both saw the new moon should both travel to testify. It explains that this is a backup plan, not a way for them to form a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives usually cannot testify together as one pair of witnesses. Still, both should go, because if one turns out to be unfit, the other is available to pair with an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, which marks the start of a new משנה
They join together to form a valid pair of witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying father and son count as a pair. It says the opposite: they cannot join each other, and each goes only as a backup.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אָב וּבְנוֹ שֶׁרָאוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ — יֵלְכוּ.
phrases.english: A father and his son who saw the new moon should go.
Not that they join together with one another,
but so that if one of them is disqualified,
the second can join together with another witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָב וּבְנוֹ שֶׁרָאוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ — יֵלְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic: relatives as witnesses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives cannot form a pair for עדות החודש, but both should go so each can serve as a backup with another witness.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says relatives are valid for testimony about the month
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says a father, his son, and all relatives are valid witnesses for עדות החודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: A father and his son and all relatives are valid for testimony about the new moon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He holds that relatives may testify together about the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion applies the normal rule that relatives are unfit to testify together. רבי שמעון says עדות החודש is an exception to that rule, so a father and son could even form the pair themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony about seeing the new moon

steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion sets up the גמרא's search for a source. Why would עדות החודש be different from all other testimony?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
A father and his son and all relatives
are valid for testimony about the new moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אָב וּבְנוֹ וְכׇל הַקְּרוֹבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives are valid to testify together for עדות החודש.

steps.title: The story of טוביה הרופא, his son, and his freed slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells about טוביה הרופא, who saw the new moon with his son and his freed slave. The כהנים accepted him and his son but rejected the slave. The בית דין accepted him and the slave but rejected the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a story with טוביה the doctor, who saw the new moon in ירושלים, together with his son and his freed slave. The כהנים accepted him and his son and disqualified his slave. When they came before the בית דין, the judges accepted him and his slave and disqualified his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי tells a story in which two groups each disqualified a different witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים rejected the freed slave but had no problem with father and son together. The בית דין did the reverse: they accepted the freed slave and rejected the son. The בית דין's ruling matches the first opinion in the משנה, that relatives cannot testify together.

keyTerms.meaning: The court that set the month

steps.whatToRemember: The בית דין rejected the son because he was related to his father, but accepted the freed slave.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Toviyya the doctor
who saw the new moon in Jerusalem,
he and his son and his freed slave,
and the priests accepted him and his son
and disqualified his slave.
And when they came before the court,
they accepted him and his slave,
and disqualified his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּטוֹבִיָּה הָרוֹפֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story about relatives testifying on the new moon
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, the בית דין disqualified a son testifying with his father and accepted a freed slave.

steps.title: רבי לוי's source for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains רבי שמעון's reason from the פסוק 'החודש הזה לכם,' spoken to משה and אהרן: this testimony is valid even from 'you,' brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי לוי said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון? It is written: 'And ה׳ said to משה and to אהרן in the land of מצרים, saying: This month shall be for you.' This means that this testimony will be valid with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי לוי gives the פסוק behind רבי שמעון's view that relatives are valid for עדות החודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of setting the month was said to both משה and אהרן, who were brothers. The word 'לכם' ('for you') is read to mean that this testimony is valid even from people like you, relatives. That makes עדות החודש an exception to the usual rule against relatives testifying together.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, which marks the start of the גמרא's discussion
'For you', the word the derivation is built on

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a source in the Torah for treating עדות החודש differently from ordinary testimony.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Levi said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron
in the land of Egypt, saying:
This month shall be for you'
this testimony shall be valid with you.
phrases.notes: 'You' here means משה and אהרן, who were brothers. So even relatives are valid for this testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by giving a source for רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'החודש הזה לכם,' said to the brothers משה and אהרן, teach that relatives are valid for עדות החודש.

steps.title: How the רבנן read 'לכם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן understand 'החודש הזה לכם'. They read it as: this testimony is handed over to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they read the פסוק? They say it means: this testimony shall be handed over to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who forbid relatives to testify together, explain the פסוק that רבי שמעון used. It answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned from 'לכם' that even brothers like משה and אהרן can testify together. The רבנן read 'לכם' differently: setting the months is entrusted to you, meaning the leaders of the generation. So the פסוק is about who holds the authority, not about relatives as witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; the majority opinion that argues on רבי שמעון

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: how do the רבנן explain the פסוק 'החודש הזה לכם' that רבי שמעון just used?

phrases.english: This testimony shall be handed over to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק that step 6 used for רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן interpret 'החודש הזה לכם' if they do not learn from it that relatives are valid.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק means that the authority over this testimony is entrusted to 'you', the leaders.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the story of טוביה הרופא from the משנה. רב חנן בר רבא then rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי told of an incident with טוביה הרופא, and so on. רב חנן בר רבא said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points back to the story of טוביה הרופא in the משנה. רב חנן בר רבא then gives a ruling that relatives are valid, like רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story of טוביה shows the בית דין turning down his son, which supports the view that relatives cannot testify together. Even so, רב חנן בר רבא rules like רבי שמעון. That sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'and so on'; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said
There was an incident with Toviyah the doctor, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the story from the משנה in step 5. The 'etc.' means 'finish the quote yourself.'

phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַעֲשֶׂה בְּטוֹבִיָּה הָרוֹפֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's story and opens a new discussion about the final הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: relatives may testify together for עדות החודש.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא objects. רבי יוסי held the other view, and there was a real incident, so how can the הלכה follow רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to רב חנן בר רבא: you have רבי יוסי, and an actual incident, and you still say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב חנן בר רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two strikes against ruling like רבי שמעון. First, רבי יוסי is usually followed against his colleagues. Second, there was a real case where the בית דין actually turned down the son, and an actual ruling carries great weight.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רב

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to Rav Chanan bar Rava:
Rabbi Yosei, and an actual incident,
phrases.notes: Two reasons packed into two words: רבי יוסי's opinion is usually followed, and a real case was decided that way.

phrases.english: and you say the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנן בר רבא's ruling like רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי is usually followed, and an actual incident was decided against רבי שמעון's view.

steps.title: רב never objected
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא answers that he often said this ruling in front of רב, and רב never said a word against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: but many times I said in front of רב that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, and he never said anything to me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רבא defends his ruling. He points out that his teacher רב heard it many times and stayed quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is that רב's silence means רב agreed. If the ruling were wrong, רב would have corrected him.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין אֲמַרִית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
phrases.english: But many times I said before Rav
that the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon
and he did not say anything at all to me!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין אֲמַרִית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ruling against רב הונא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a teacher's silent approval
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling goes against רבי יוסי and an actual incident.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב heard the ruling and never objected, so he must have agreed.

steps.title: How did you learn the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks how רב חנן learned the משנה. He answers that he learned it with the names switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: how did you learn it? He answered: the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks which version of the משנה רב חנן learned. רב חנן answers that he had the names reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חנן's version, the view that our משנה gives to רבי שמעון (relatives are valid) was said by רבי יוסי. The opposite view and the story were in רבי שמעון's name. This changes what his ruling actually meant.

phrases.english: He said to him: How did you learn it?
He said to him: The opposite way.
phrases.notes: In his version the names רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון were switched around.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי תָּנֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the text רב חנן learned, to test his claim from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the משנה רב חנן learned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learned it with the names of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון reversed.

steps.title: That is why רב stayed quiet
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that רב said nothing because, in רב חנן's reversed version, the ruling was correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: that is why רב did not say anything to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows that רב's silence does not prove that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in our version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רב חנן said 'like רבי שמעון', רב heard it as the view in רבי שמעון's name in רב חנן's text, which matches our רבי יוסי. So רב was really agreeing with what our משנה calls רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of this, that is why

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a disagreement over which view is correct. רב was agreeing with the view that relatives are disqualified; the name attached to it was simply switched in רב חנן's version.

phrases.english: He said to him: That is why
he did not say anything at all to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אֲמַר לָךְ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in step 11 to knock down the proof from step 10.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב was hearing the ruling according to a reversed text, so his silence supported the opposite view.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: טבי son of מרי טבי said in the name of מר עוקבא, who said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a separate ruling, passed down from שמואל, that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון (as named in our משנה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed that רב's silence actually backed the view that relatives are disqualified, because רב חנן's 'רבי שמעון' was our רבי יוסי. שמואל, by contrast, rules outright like our רבי שמעון, that relatives are valid. So the two great masters, רב and שמואל, end up on opposite sides.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on שמואל's teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רב (through רב חנן's reversed version) held that relatives are disqualified, while שמואל rules like רבי שמעון that relatives are valid for עדות החודש.

phrases.english: Tavi son of Mari Tavi said
Mar Ukva said, Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר טָבִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּמָרִי טָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 shows רב actually held relatives are disqualified, brings שמואל's opposing ruling in favor of רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון that relatives are valid for עדות החודש, in contrast to רב's view as uncovered in step 12.

steps.title: List of disqualified witnesses
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists people who cannot testify: dice players, lenders who charge interest, pigeon racers, merchants of שביעית produce, and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the disqualified ones: one who plays with dice, those who lend with interest, those who race pigeons, those who trade in שביעית produce, and slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists categories of people who are not valid witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these people make money in a dishonest or forbidden way, like gambling, taking interest, or trading in שביעית produce, so they are not trusted. Slaves are on the list for a different reason, not because of how they earn money.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who race pigeons for bets

phrases.english: Mishnah:
These are the disqualified ones:
one who plays with dice,
and those who lend with interest,
and those who race pigeons,
and merchants of Sabbatical-year produce,
and slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן הַפְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about which witnesses are disqualified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gamblers, lenders who charge interest, pigeon racers, merchants of שביעית produce, and slaves are disqualified witnesses.

steps.title: The general rule: compared to a woman
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a general rule: any testimony for which a woman is not valid, these people are not valid for either.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: any testimony for which a woman is not valid, they too are not valid for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with one general rule that sums up the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is valid in only a few special cases, such as testifying that a husband died, and is not valid in most kinds of testimony. The people on the list follow the same pattern. Wherever a woman is not accepted, they are not accepted either.

phrases.english: This is the general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֵדוּת שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לָהּ,
phrases.english: any testimony for which a woman is not valid,
they too are not valid for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the list from step 14 with one general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people on the list are disqualified for any testimony for which a woman is disqualified.

steps.title: Wherever a woman is valid, they are valid too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's rule in reverse: testimony a woman may give, these disqualified people may also give.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: wherever a woman cannot testify, these people cannot either. That implies the opposite too: wherever a woman CAN testify, these people can also testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the last line of the משנה. This sets up רב אשי's practical conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gave the negative side: where a woman is invalid, they are invalid. The גמרא points out that this also teaches the positive side. Their status is linked to a woman's in both directions.

phrases.english: Gemara
This implies: testimony for which a woman is valid
these too are valid for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לָהּ אַף הֵן כְּשֵׁירִין לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers the positive side from the משנה's general rule in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualified people listed in the משנה are valid wherever a woman's testimony is valid.

steps.title: A rabbinic robber may testify for a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that someone who is a גזלן only by rabbinic law may testify where a woman may, such as testimony allowing a woman to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This teaches us that a person who counts as a robber only by rabbinic law is valid to give testimony about a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns the inference from step 16 into a practical rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of the people listed in the משנה, like dice players and pigeon racers, are disqualified only because the Rabbis treat them as robbers. Since step 16 showed they are valid wherever a woman is valid, רב אשי concludes that every גזלן דדבריהם may testify in עדות אשה, where even a woman is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is to say (introducing a rule learned from a source)
A robber by rabbinic law, not by Torah law
Testimony that lets a woman remarry

steps.whatToRemember: A גזלן דדבריהם is disqualified only in a limited way. He may still testify wherever a woman's testimony is accepted, like עדות אשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical halachic boundary: rabbinic disqualification does not block testimony that frees a woman to remarry.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said
This is to say
one who is a robber by their (the Rabbis') words
are valid for testimony concerning a woman.
phrases.notes: This means testimony that her husband died, so she is allowed to remarry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical halacha from the inference in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גזלן דדבריהם is valid to testify in עדות אשה.

steps.title: Carrying a witness who cannot walk, and taking sticks for protection
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a witness of the new moon who cannot walk may be carried on a donkey or even in a bed, and witnesses may carry sticks if bandits are waiting for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone saw the new moon but cannot walk, people bring him on a donkey, even in a bed. If people are lying in wait to attack them, they may carry sticks in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It continues the topic of witnesses traveling to בית דין, even on שבת, and lists what they are allowed to do to get there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting the testimony to בית דין is so important that normal שבת limits are pushed aside. The witness may be carried, and the group may carry weapons for safety.

phrases.english: Mishnah
One who saw the new moon
and is not able to walk
they bring him on the donkey
even in a bed.
And if someone lies in wait for them
they take sticks in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁרָאָה אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַלֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about the travel of the witnesses to בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who cannot walk may be carried, and witnesses may carry sticks for protection.

steps.title: Taking food for a long trip, and the source for breaking שבת
steps.stepSummary: On a long trip the witnesses may carry food, because they may break שבת for a journey of up to a night and a day. The source is 'אשר תקראו אותם במועדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the road is long, they take food in their hands. For a journey of a night and a day, people break שבת and go out to testify about the new moon, as it says: 'These are the festivals of ה׳ which you shall declare in their proper time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more allowance, carrying food, and then gives the reason and the פסוק behind all of these allowances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is a trip of up to a night and a day; that much travel justifies breaking שבת. The פסוק stresses 'במועדם', in their proper time. The festivals must be set on time, so the witnesses' testimony overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A journey of a night and a day

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses of the new moon may break שבת for a journey of up to a night and a day. They may be carried, carry sticks, and carry food, because the festivals must be set 'במועדם'.

phrases.english: And if it was a long road
they take food in their hands
since for a journey of a night and a day
they break שבת
and go out for testimony of the new moon
as it is said:
"These are the festivals of ה׳
which you shall declare in their proper time."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיְתָה דֶּרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה לוֹקְחִין בְּיָדָם מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה and gives the reason and source for all the allowances.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may carry food and break שבת for a journey of up to a night and a day, based on 'אשר תקראו אותם במועדם'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing ארבעה ראשי שנים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first chapter of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter ארבעה ראשי שנים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally ends the first chapter of the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the legal discussion. It is the traditional way of finishing a chapter and expressing the wish to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: Name of the first chapter of ראש השנה

phrases.english: We will return to you
Arba'ah Rashei Shanim (Four New Years).

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ אַרְבָּעָה רָאשֵׁי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of ראש השנה is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: an unknown witness needs someone to vouch for him
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if בית דין does not recognize the witness of the new moon, his town sends another person with him to vouch for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court does not know the witness, they send another person with him to testify that he is reliable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a new משנה. It teaches what happens when the witness who saw the new moon is a stranger to בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין can only accept testimony about the new moon from a witness they trust. If they do not know him, someone who does know him must come along and confirm that he is a kosher witness. This extra person is not testifying about the moon, only about the witness himself.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognize or know (here, that the witness is reliable)
To testify about him, to vouch for him

steps.confusionAlert: The extra person is not a second witness to the moon. He only vouches that the first witness is trustworthy.

phrases.english: If they do not recognize him —
phrases.notes: 'They' is the בית דין in ירושלים, and 'him' is the witness who saw the new moon.

phrases.english: they send another with him to testify about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינָן מַכִּירִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן closing the first פרק in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unknown witness of the new moon must be accompanied by someone who vouches for his reliability.

steps.title: History of the rule: the בייתוסים caused a stricter enactment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that originally testimony about the new moon was accepted from anyone, but after the בייתוסים caused damage, the Sages made a תקנה to accept testimony only from known people.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, the court accepted new-moon testimony from anybody. After the בייתוסים caused trouble, the חכמים ruled that testimony would be accepted only from people the court knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by giving the background for the rule it just taught. It tells us the rule was not always this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic law any kosher person could testify about the new moon without being known to בית דין. Only after the בייתוסים damaged the system did the Sages add a תקנה requiring known witnesses. This explains why step 21 requires a person to vouch for a stranger.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony about seeing the new moon
A group that rejected the teachings of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: The requirement that a witness be known to בית דין is a rabbinic תקנה, made because of the בייתוסים. Originally testimony was accepted from anyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the stricter rule of step 21 is a protective enactment, not the original basic law.

phrases.english: At first they would accept
testimony about the new month from any person.
Once the Baytusim caused corruption,
they enacted that they would not accept testimony
except from those whom they recognize.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ מִכׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical reason behind the rule in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the בייתוסים, the Sages enacted that new-moon testimony is accepted only from known witnesses.

steps.title: What does 'another' mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means by 'another' person, and begins to suggest that it might mean just one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'another' mean? One person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה by asking about the word 'another' from step 21. This line is setting up the next move, and the question continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'another' in the singular, which sounds like one person is enough to vouch for the witness. The גמרא is starting to test that reading, since one person is normally not enough to establish testimony. The full question and its answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara: What is meant by 'another'?
If it means one person,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's wording from step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many people the משנה means by 'another,' starting with the possibility that it means only one.
